segments.text: Good afternoon, this is Aakash Vani and I am Sairam Uchthaba with the mid-day news.
The headlines
Union Home Minister Amit Shah calls upon police forces to work towards eliminating drug
menace by end of 2029, says it damages future generations.
CBI takes over probe into killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Punjab.

U.S. President Donald Trump says India and United States are close to reaching trade
deal.

degrees Celsius threshold.
And an Asian Paragames India achieve spectacular podium sweep, clinching gold, silver and
bronze in Men's Shortput F-46 event today.
And now the news in detail.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah today said that the government has set a target to eliminate
the drug menace from India by 31 December 2029.
Speaking at the Police Commemoration Day ceremony at the National Police Memorial in New Delhi,
Mr Shah called upon police forces across the country to work towards eliminating narcotics
by the end of 2029.
He said the drug menace is a serious challenge as it damages future generations,
relations, places an undue burden on the economy and provides financial support to organizations
involved in anti-national activities.
Drugs are a serious menace that weaken our youth, undermine our economic system and provide
support to anti-national organizations.
Our Honourable Prime Minister, Srinarendra Modiji, has vowed to eradicate the menace
of drugs and today I call upon all police personnel to stand united and resolve to
fulfill this mission and protect the future of our next generation.
The Home Minister said that the country has liberated itself from the menace of
Naxalism on 31 March this year, paying tributes to police personnel who laid down
their lives in the service of the nation. Mr Shah said that the country had endured
the pain of Naxalism from 1981 until March 2026. During this period, more than
3,600 security personnel, and nearly 13,000 innocent civilians lost their lives. Home
Minister Shah said a total of 36,852 police personnel have laid down their lives in the
line of duty since independence.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Rajstri Ekta Diva celebrations in
K. Varaya, Gujarat on 31st October, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabh
High Patel. Rashtri Ekta Divas honors Sardar Vallabhai Patel's legacy in unifying India,
promoting unity in diversity amid ongoing national challenges. Addressing a press conference
in New Delhi today, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan said that the event will highlight the
outstanding work being done by the police, Central Armed Police forces and other Central
Police organizations.
There are certain departures from the earlier practices, and these have been made with a
view with two purposes in mind.
The first purpose being to bring to the attention of the nation the extraordinary work being
done by the police and the central armed paramilitary and central police organizations.
And the second purpose was to invite the people from all parts of the country to come
them and witness these performances and events.
In Punjab, the Central Bureau of Investigation's CBI has taken over the investigation of Mansa-based
anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhotar's murder case. A team led by senior deputy inspector
general, DIG-level officer, will examine the family with all the facts and figures.
More from our correspondent.
The CBI team reached Mansa police station late last night to take over records. A
Chendigarh. According to sources, post-mortem of the victim will be conducted by a team of
doctors in BGI Chendigarh and inquiry will be done by a Chendigarh-based magistrate.
The action came within hours of the Union Home Minister Amish Shah's assurance of the
CBI probe when he met Parvinder Singh's family during his day-long visit to Punjab yesterday.
Jhota was shot dead by a chemist Ashmi Kumar last week when he confronted the
chemist for selling synthetic drugs.
The home minister had also met another anti-drug activist Vikramjit Singh's family in Gurdaspur
who was also allegedly killed by drug traffickers for objecting to sale of drugs.
Shri Shah also assured justice to the family of Gulzar Singh, who allegedly committed suicide
in Senguru recently when his pleas were not heard by the state government against
the sale of drugs which made his son an addict.
Rajesh Bali, Aakashwani News, Jalandhar
President Draupadi Murmur has emphasised the need to economically empower artists and encourage
them to broaden their horizons and sharpen their artistic skills to compete at the national
and international levels. Speaking at the awards ceremony of 65th National Exhibition of Art
in New Delhi today, the president said that art reflects the culture of a country. She
also emphasised the need to provide artists with additional guidance and training to help
them adapt to changing times and participate in competitions.
President Murmu said that it is the collective responsibility to support artists in achieving
doing economic progress and adapting to changing times.
The 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference began at Bharat Mantapam in New Delhi this afternoon
to promote AgriVoltaics as a commercially viable and farmer-centric model to strengthen food
and energy security. In AgriVoltaics, land is used simultaneously for both agricultural
activities and solar energy generation. Union New and Renewable Energy Minister Prahlad
Joshi and Agriculture and Farmers' well-feminist Shivraj Singh Johan inaugurated the conference.
The theme of the three-day conference is Powering the Global South.
The Indian Army and the Indo-Tibetan border police ITBP held a coordination conference
at Chushul in eastern Ladakh to discuss border management and issues of mutual interest.
The conference emphasised jointness, coordination and co-operation between the two forces
to strengthen border management and safeguard the nation's frontiers.
The Army's Fire and Fury Corps, responsible for military operations in Ladakh, shared
the information in a social media post.
The interaction reaffirmed the commitment of the Indian Army and ITBB to work closely
together to address border-related challenges and enhance cooperation in the region.
United States Secretary of State Marku Rubio has arrived in Jamnagar on the second leg
of his crucial three-divisit to India.
Secretary Rubio's schedule to tour the iconic Reliance Industries Refinery complex, the world's
largest single-location crude oil refining facility. Following the inspection, the top
U.S. diplomat is expected to hold a high-level meeting with Reliance Chairman Mukesh Ambani.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
US President Donald Trump has said that India and the US are close to reaching a trade deal.
Speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, he said the agreement would be different from
earlier trade pacts. Mr. Trump said both countries wanted to reach an agreement. His remarks
talks came during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India, where he discussed
strengthening bilateral ties in trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people relations.
Earlier this month, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met U.S. Trade Representative James Sengriya
in Milwaukee and Washington to discuss the details of the proposed agreement.
India and the U.S. had announced in February the finalization of a framework for the
first phase of their bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in U.S. tariff policies have
led to further negotiations on the pact.
The United Nations Environment Programme has warned that the world must cut greenhouse gas
emissions by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, compared with 2025 levels to
minimize global warming beyond 1.5 degree Celsius and bring temperatures back to that
threshold by the end of the century. In its report titled, The Emissions Gap Report 2026,
the United Nations Environment Program, UNEP, said, the immediate priority must be to limit
the scale and duration of this overshoot and pursue a pathway that could return warming
to or below 1.5 degree Celsius by 2100. It said global warming could worsen beyond
want earlier projections, with the United States withdrawal from the Paris Climate Agreement
contributing to the rise.
It said U.S. recorded the largest increase in greenhouse gas emissions among the world's
20 major economies last year.
Its emissions rose by 133 million tons of carbon dioxide, equivalent driven by higher
electricity demand, and increased coal-fired power generation.
India has opposed the use of human rights as a political tool to selectively target
countries on the basis of unverified allegations.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, Indian Representative Barkha Tamrakar
said human rights must not be used for political pressure or selective country targeting.
Ms. Tamrakar said India remains willing to clarify specific, properly documented cases
through established channels.
The United Nations is launching an initiative to address risks posed by the growing
use of artificial intelligence in military operations, including potential threats
to human control and nuclear security. The UN Institute for Disarmament Research plans
to launch an international forum tomorrow to bring together key stakeholders to discuss
military applications of AI. Mr. Robin Jai's head of the Geneva-based
Institute warned that the margin for human judgment is increasingly narrow, including
in the nuclear domain. He also said AI was increasingly being used in early warning
warning systems, intelligence gathering and reconnaissance, making it difficult to determine
when human control could be compromised.
India achieved a spectacular podium sweep at the Asian Paragames in Aichi Nagoya, Japan
as Sachin Sarje Rao Khiladi, Mohammad Yasir and Parveen clinched gold, silver and bronze
respectively in the men's short put F-46 event today.
Khiladi led the Indian triumph with a record-breaking throw of 15.87 meters.
Yasir secured the silver with a best throw of 15.06 metres, while Praveen claimed bronze
with 14.94 metres. These athletes also recorded their season best performances, making it
a memorable clean sweep for India on the podium.
A report
India's Praveen Kumar won gold in the men's high jump T-44-64, with the game's record
while Bunty clinched silver in the same event. Praveen sailed over 2.05 metres to
the gold while Bunty produced a personal best of 1.92m to take the silver. Ayush Varma also won
gold medal in the men's short put F-53 event today, adding a second medal to his tally.
Ayush produced a throw-off 8.16m in his fifth attempt to take the top spot.
Teenage Indian pair of para-archers Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag clinched a silver medal
after losing in the compound women's doubles final today. Sheetal and Payal went down
won 141-150 to the Chinese duo of Shu Shui Cheng and Zhao Jiyang.
Sheetal had won a silver medal in this event in the last edition of the game, partnering
Sarita Devi in the men's 100m T-35 event, Anubhav Chaudhary secured a bronze medal.
He clocked a personal best of 12.72 seconds to win the medal.
Rakesh Bhai Bhatt also won bronze medal in the men's 100m T-37 event.
With Puneet Saxena's report, Jigasa Pandey, Akash Chawani News, Delhi.
The world-renowned Mysuru Dasara Festival will culminate with Vijay Hadashmi's ceremony
today.
The ceremony will be marked by a magnificent Jambosavari procession later in the afternoon
from Mysore Palace to Bani Mantap, more from our correspondent.
Thousands have gathered in Mysuru today to witness the Vijay Dasami celebrations
on the 11th day of Dasara, the grand Vijay Dasami procession with comparison elephants,
folk dance troupes, music bands, tableaux and marched by police and defence personnel
is a spectacle to watch. At around 4 p.m. today, floral offerings will be made to the idol of
Goddess Chamundeshwari, adorned in 750 kg golden houda, placed on Majestic 54-year-old Tuskar,
Prashanta. Thereafter, the procession will begin from Ambavila's palace to Banimantap. Kerala
Chief Minister V. D. Satishan and Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy will be present
on this occasion. The festivities will end with torchlight parade and fireworks tonight.
India's UNESCO tentative list of world heritage sites has been expanded to 78, with five new
additions, including Udaiguri case in Madhya Pradesh and a joint India-South Africa proposal
featuring sites associated with Mahatma Gandhi's Satya Graham movement.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
